Dear Dr. Philip:

ability<-fscores(mymirt, method="EAP",response.pattern = data,QMC=TRUE)
Error in rep.int(rep.int(seq_len(nx), rep.int(rep.fac, nx)), orep) : vector is too large
In addition: Warning message:
High-dimensional models should use quasi-Monte Carlo integration. Pass QMC=TRUE 

  The model is a 4-dimensional PCM.
         mymodel<-"F1=1-4
                   F2=5-13
                   F3=14-17
                   F4=18-22
                  COV=F1*F2*F3*F4"
 
         mymodel<-mirt.model(mymodel)
 
         mymirt<-mirt(data,mymodel,itemtype="Rasch",method = "MHRM")

    How can I solve this problem if I want to get EAP estimates? 

    Thank You.

Best regards.

Here is the whole script

> library(mirt)

> library(MASS)

> vmatrix<-c(c(1,0,0,0),c(0,1,0,0),c(0,0,1,0),c(0,0,0,1))

> sigma<-matrix(vmatrix,4,4)

>

> ####40 binary item

> set.seed(11)

> theta<-mvrnorm(2000,c(0,0,0,0),sigma)

> d<-matrix(rep(rnorm(10,0,1),4),40,1,byrow = T)*1.702

> a<-matrix(c(runif(10,0.5,2),rep(0,30),

+             rep(0,10),runif(10,0.5,2),rep(0,20),

+             rep(0,20),runif(10,0.5,2),rep(0,10),

+             rep(0,30),runif(10,0.5,2)),

+             40,4)

> binary.data<-simdata(a,d[,1],itemtype = '2PL',Theta=theta)

>

> binary.model<-"

+ F1=1-10

+ F2=11-20

+ F3=21-30

+ F4=31-40

+ "

> binary.model<-mirt.model(binary.model)

> binary<-mirt(binary.data,binary.model,itemtype="2PL",method = "MHRM")

Stage 3 = 93, LL = -47878.0, AR(1.00) = [0.16], gam = 0.0060, Max-Change = 0.0006

 

Calculating log-likelihood...

> binary.ability<-fscores(binary, method="EAP",response.pattern = binary.data,QMC=TRUE)

Error in rep.int(rep.int(seq_len(nx), rep.int(rep.fac, nx)), orep) :

  vector is too large

In addition: Warning message:

High-dimensional models should use quasi-Monte Carlo integration. Pass QMC=TRUE

> ####40 poly item

> vmatrix<-c(c(1,0,0,0),c(0,1,0,0),c(0,0,1,0),c(0,0,0,1))

> sigma<-matrix(vmatrix,4,4)

> set.seed(11)

> theta<-mvrnorm(2000,c(0,0,0,0),sigma)

> diff<- rbind(t(apply(matrix(runif(10*4, 0, 1), 10), 1, cumsum)),

+                 t(apply(matrix(runif(10*4, 0, 1), 10), 1, cumsum)),

+                 t(apply(matrix(runif(10*4, 0, 1), 10), 1, cumsum)),

+                 t(apply(matrix(runif(10*4, 0, 1), 10), 1, cumsum)))

> diff<- -(diff - rowMeans(diff))

> d <- diff + rnorm(40)

> a<-matrix(c(rep(1,10),rep(0,30),

+             rep(0,10),rep(1,10),rep(0,20),

+             rep(0,20),rep(1,10),rep(0,10),

+             rep(0,30),rep(1,10)),

+           40,4)

> poly.data<-simdata(a,d,itemtype = 'gpcm',Theta=theta)

>

> poly.model<-"

+ F1=1-10

+ F2=11-20

+ F3=21-30

+ F4=31-40

+ "

> poly.model<-mirt.model(poly.model)

> poly.mirt<-mirt(poly.data,poly.model,itemtype="Rasch",method = "MHRM")

Stage 3 = 19, LL = -91194.0, AR(0.40) = [0.14], gam = 0.0203, Max-Change = 0.0009

 

Calculating log-likelihood...

> poly.ability<-fscores(poly.mirt, method="EAP",response.pattern = poly.data,QMC=TRUE)

Error in rep.int(rep.int(seq_len(nx), rep.int(rep.fac, nx)), orep) :

  vector is too large

In addition: Warning message:

High-dimensional models should use quasi-Monte Carlo integration. Pass QMC=TRUE
The error

Error in rep.int(rep.int(seq_len(nx), rep.int(rep.fac, nx)), orep) :

  vector is too large

occurs in the stage for estimating ability parameters.
It seems that it only occurs when
  • there are over 3 factors,
  • and the response pattern argument is included,
  • and "EAP" method is used,
  • and "QMC=TRUE" is passed.

Kind regards.

Thank you. When I pass this on the latest dev version:

binary.ability<-fscores(binary, method="EAP", QMC=TRUE)

I get no errors. Likely because the QMC methods have been better optimised for efficiency and effectiveness. You can try updating from Github directly at this point, otherwise you could wait a few weeks until I release the next major version to CRAN. 

That being said, I highly recommend you use method='MAP' rather than EAP for high dimensional factor scores. Even with Monte Carlo integration they still can be an issue, while iterative methods like MAP don't suffer from integration problems. Cheers. 

Phil
